subject: technology
topic: Your phone weakens your thinking even when you are not using it
angle: While some experiments suggest a 'brain drain' effect on cognitive capacity and working memory, a large meta-analysis found no significant effect on cognitive outcomes.
title: The Cost of Presence

hooks.text: Does your phone drain your brain when you are not using it?
You think you are ignoring your phone. The evidence shows it is still affecting you.
Your smartphone dependence is creating a constant cognitive cost.
A dark screen on a wooden table.

reveal.headline: Your phone drains your brain even when it is silent.
reveal.body: The mere presence of a smartphone reduces available cognitive capacity. This effect is most significant for those with high smartphone dependence.

explain.headline: The evidence on this effect is mixed.
explain.body: While some studies show reduced cognitive capacity, a meta-analysis found no significant effect on many other cognitive functions. Research in this area has poor statistical power.

matters.headline: Your environment shapes your focus.
matters.body: That may be why you feel less capable of concentrating when your device is nearby. It may be a constant drain on your mental resources.

example.headline: A phone sits on the desk.
example.body: You are trying to write a report. The screen is dark. You do not touch it. Your focus still flickers. Your mind remains divided between the work and the device nearby.

question.headline: Where is your focus going?
question.body: Think about the objects on your desk.

claims.text: The mere presence of a smartphone reduces available cognitive capacity, even when people successfully avoid the temptation to check them.
claims.quote: Results from two experiments indicate that even when people are successful at maintaining sustained attention—as when avoiding the temptation to check their phones—the mere presence of these devices reduces available cognitive capacity.

claims.text: A meta-analysis found that the mere presence of a smartphone negatively impacts working memory capacity, but has no significant effect on other cognitive functions.
claims.quote: Working memory capacity was negatively impacted by the mere presence of a smartphone, while results for the remaining cognitive functions produced null summary effects.

claims.text: Participants with higher positive urgency showed increased cognitive interference in a silent-mode smartphone condition compared to a turned-off smartphone condition.
claims.quote: The results showed that participants with higher positive urgency presented increased cognitive interference (reflected by poorer task performance) in the "silent-mode smartphone" condition compared with participants in the "turned-off smartphone" condition.

claims.text: The cognitive costs of a smartphone's presence are highest for people who have a high level of smartphone dependence.
claims.quote: Moreover, these cognitive costs are highest for those highest in smartphone dependence.

claims.text: An experiment on participants aged 20-34 showed that the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance.
claims.quote: The results of the conducted experiment imply that the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance, which supports the hypothesis of the smartphone presence using limited cognitive resources.

verdict: The evidence is mixed, with some studies showing reduced cognitive capacity and others finding no significant impact on performance.
caveat: The research is characterized by substantial methodological heterogeneity and generally poor statistical power.
caption:
Your phone may be hijacking your cognitive capacity without you ever touching it.

Research shows that the mere presence of a smartphone can reduce working memory, though a meta-analysis found no significant effect on other functions. The current evidence is mixed and limited by poor statistical power.
